A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Distributional Active Inference. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original RiverSwim experiments, continuous-control evaluations, a DAIF-SAC ablation and training-time measurements in Section 6 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark scores, learning curves, ablation outcomes and timing measurements.

M1.justification: The DAIF procedure, priors, critic objective and actor–critic updates remain unchanged. The loss and implementation summary added to Section 4 already appear in v1 Appendix B.2.4 and Algorithm 7.

E1.justification: Both evaluate RiverSwim and Latent RiverSwim, seven EvoGym environments, seven state-based DMC environments and five DMC Vision environments. v2 summarizes existing appendix coverage more explicitly.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: PSRL-PI and IQQL for tabular experiments; DRND, DSAC and DTD3 for continuous control, with DrQ-v2 additionally used for vision. The DAIF-SAC comparison is retained.

E3.justification: Appendix B retains the interaction budgets, architectures, preprocessing, optimization settings and evaluation procedures. Visitation frequency, AULC, final return and ranking metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: The horizon comparisons, DAIF-SAC ablation in Table 6 and wall-clock analysis were already present in v1. v2 adds interpretations of these analyses without adding or changing their experimental evidence.

E5.justification: Both report 50 tabular repetitions, 10 repetitions for EvoGym and state-based DMC, and five for DMC Vision. Standard-error shading and standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores, rankings, learning-curve data and raw timings are unchanged. Section 6 newly states DSAC and DRND overheads of 26% and 37% relative to DTD3, calculated from timings already reported in v1 Appendix B.2.5.

T1.justification: Section 3 qualifies the previously unqualified posterior-mean Bayes-optimality statement by specifying squared loss. The principal lemmas, contraction bound and appendix proofs are retained. Appendix A.7 relocates the existing process-measure construction, and the new main-text loss equation repeats the earlier appendix.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims: reformulating AIF, introducing push-forward RL and implementing DAIF without explicit transition-model learning. Headline performance and convergence claims are retained.

C2.justification: v2 attributes bottleneck compression to L_E rather than L_D and explains how excessive compression can increase decoder sensitivity. It expands the proposed exploration mechanism through inverse-gamma uncertainty and adds explicit limitations: no explicit EFE or separated epistemic/instrumental terms, and an architecture-set rather than automatically learned bottleneck.

D1.justification: Detailed architectures, hyperparameters, update procedures, hardware and resource links remain unchanged in Appendix B. The additional main-text loss and TD3-style implementation summary restate information already supplied in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Berger (1985) and removes Eberhardt and Scheines (2007). Expanded Section 5 summaries largely reproduce distributional-RL and exploration positioning already present in Appendix C, with a more specific explanation of DAIF's implicit exploration.

P1.justification: v2 tightens prose, expands notation and explanatory passages, renames Section 5 to Related Work, separates tabular and continuous-control summaries, and moves the explicit trajectory construction to Appendix A.7. The overall narrative structure and most appendix text remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds conceptual Figure 1, introduces distinct method markers and thinner lines in tabular plots, revises the state-abstraction caption, and repositions existing figures and tables. The experimental plots retain their underlying data and the tables retain their structure.

improvement.justification: v2 improves accessibility through the conceptual diagram and clearer summaries, while the squared-loss qualification and explicit AIF and bottleneck limitations improve precision. Experiments and principal proofs remain unchanged, and the expanded exploration explanation receives no new validating analysis, so the overall gain is limited.
